markscheme.html:
A

For the first harmonic in a pipe closed at one end and open at the other, there is a displacement node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end. There are no other nodes along the length of the pipe. All points within a single loop of a standing wave (i.e., between two adjacent nodes) oscillate in phase. Since the middle point and the open end are both within the first loop, their phase difference is 0.

question.html: A first harmonic standing wave is formed in a pipe with one end open and one end closed. What is the phase difference between the middle point of the pipe and its open end?
